summary: The opening of the Charaka Samhita, Sūtrasthāna 1: the chapter's announcement, Bharadvāja's search for long life, the line of Āyurveda from Brahmā to Indra, and the sages who gathered on the Himālaya. Units 1 to 10.

unitSummaries.Chapter 1: How Āyurveda passed from Brahmā to Indra, why the sages gathered on the Himālaya, and who they were.

concepts.title: १. अथातो दीर्घञ्जीवितीयम्

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · गद्य १। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

words.gram: पु. द्वितीया ए.व.; नाम-विशेषण, इससे बना: ‘दीर्घं जीवितम्’ (अलुक्, -ईय)

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: अब, इसलिए, हम ‘दीर्घञ्जीवितीय’ नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called Dirghanjivitiya ('On Long Life').

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: यह अध्याय का आरम्भ-वाक्य है; इसी साँचे में सूत्रस्थान के अध्याय खुलते हैं। ‘अथ’ आरम्भ का सूचक है, ‘अतः’ का अर्थ ‘इस कारण से’ है। ‘व्याख्यास्यामः’ उत्तम पुरुष बहुवचन है, यानी ‘हम खोलकर समझाएँगे’। अध्याय का नाम ‘दीर्घञ्जीवितीय’ अगले श्लोक के पहले शब्दों ‘दीर्घं जीवितम्’ से बना है।

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: व्याख्यास्यामः ← वि + आ + √ख्या (कहना): ‘खोलकर कहना’। जोड़ें: व्याख्या, आख्यान, ख्यात।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अ/आ + अ/आ → आ: अथ + अतः → अथातः (पाठ में अथातो: विसर्ग घोष ‘द’ से पहले ‘ओ’ बनता है, अतः + दी… → अतो दी…)। यही आ-नियम श्लोक ४ में फिर आएगा: निखिलेन + आदौ → निखिलेनादौ।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: अथातो | दीर्घञ्जीवितीयम् | अध्यायं | व्याख्यास्यामः। अथ | अतः | … | व्याख्यास्यामः = अब | इसलिए | … | हम समझाएँगे। नाम = श्लोक ३ के आरम्भिक शब्द (दीर्घं जीवितम्) + ईय (अलुक् समास)।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘दीर्घञ्जीवितीयम्’ अलुक् समास है: पहले पद ‘दीर्घम्’ की विभक्ति बनी रहती है और अन्त में ‘-ईय’ जुड़ता है।

card.rule: अथातो … अध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः = 'Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called Dīrghañjīvitīya.' अथ + अतः = अथातः. The chapter is named after the first words of verse 3, दीर्घं जीवितम्, plus the ending -ईय.
card.limits: Taking the name from verse 3 is the usual explanation of the compound; the sentence itself only names the chapter.

concepts.question: How does the chapter announce itself, and what is it called?

concepts.title: २. इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · गद्य २। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

words.gram: अव्यय (निपात); ‘ह स्म’ कथन-शैली में, यहाँ लिट् ‘आह’ के साथ

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Thus indeed spoke the venerable Atreya.

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: ‘इति’ पिछले वाक्य को उद्धरण की तरह बन्द करता है: ‘हम व्याख्या करेंगे’ कहने वाले आत्रेय हैं। ‘ह’ और ‘स्म’ निपात हैं, जो इस परम्परागत कथन-शैली में आते हैं। ‘आह’ का अर्थ ‘कहा’ है। ‘भगवान्’ आदर का विशेषण है और ‘आत्रेयः’ अत्रि के वंश का नाम है।

aids.label: कौन · किसके पास · क्यों
aids.text: वक्ता: भगवान् आत्रेय · कैसे पता: ‘इति’ उद्धरण बन्द करता है · क्रिया: आह = कहा।

aids.label: चित्र-शब्द (मेरा बनाया चित्र)
aids.text: इति = उद्धरण का बन्द चिह्न (”): ऊपर कही सारी बात आत्रेय के मुँह से।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अ + आ → आ: स्म + आह → स्माह (वही नियम जो अथ + अतः → अथातः में था)।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: इति ह | स्माह | भगवान् | आत्रेयः।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘ह’ और ‘स्म’ निपात हैं; पूरा ‘इति ह स्माह’ कथन की परम्परागत शैली है।

card.rule: इति ह स्माह भगवान् आत्रेयः = 'Thus, indeed, said the venerable Ātreya.' इति closes the opening sentence as a quotation, so 'we shall expound' is Ātreya's own statement.
card.limits: The line gives the teaching to Ātreya; it does not say who wrote it down.

concepts.question: Whose words are the opening sentence, and how does the text say so?

concepts.title: ३. दीर्घं जीवितमन्विच्छन्

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ३। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: दीर्घ जीवन की खोज करते हुए उग्र तपस्वी भरद्वाज, देवताओं के स्वामी इन्द्र को शरण देने योग्य जानकर, उनके पास गए।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Seeking a long life, Bharadvaja, a man of severe austerity, approached Indra, the lord of the immortals, having understood that he was the one fit to give refuge.

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: कथा यहीं से शुरू होती है। भरद्वाज उग्र तप वाले ऋषि हैं और उनकी चाह ‘दीर्घ जीवन’ है; इसी से अध्याय का नाम बना। वे इन्द्र के पास जाते हैं, क्योंकि उन्होंने इन्द्र को ‘शरण्य’ (शरण देने योग्य) जाना। ‘बुद्ध्वा’ (जानकर) पहले होने वाली क्रिया है और ‘उपागमत्’ (गए) बाद की; दोनों का कर्ता भरद्वाज है।

aids.label: कौन · किसके पास · क्यों
aids.text: चाह: दीर्घ जीवन · कौन: भरद्वाज · किसके पास: इन्द्र (अमरों के ईश्वर) · क्यों: शरण्य जानकर।

aids.label: कथा
aids.text: एक तपस्वी लम्बा जीवन चाहता है → इन्द्र को शरण देने योग्य जानता है → देवताओं के उन स्वामी के पास जाता है।

aids.label: चित्र-शब्द (मेरा बनाया चित्र)
aids.text: दीर्घ = बहुत लम्बी रस्सी · भरद्वाज = रस्सी खींचता साधक · इन्द्र = वज्र वाला राजा · शरण्य = राजा के हाथ की छतरी।

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: शरण्य ← शरण (शरणागत) · अन्विच्छन् ← अनु + √इष् (रूप इच्छ-, ‘इच्छा’ से जुड़ा): खोजते हुए चाहता · उपागमत् ← आगमन (उप + आ + गम्)।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अ/आ + ई → ए: अमर + ईश्वरम् → अमरेश्वरम्। वैसे ही महा + ईश → महेश।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: बुद्ध्वा (जानकर) पहले हुई क्रिया है, उपागमत् (गए) बाद की: ‘-त्वा’ वाला रूप आम तौर पर पहले की क्रिया बताता है।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: दीर्घं जीवितम् | अन्विच्छन् | भरद्वाज उपागमत् ‖ इन्द्रम् | उग्रतपा बुद्ध्वा | शरण्यम् | अमरेश्वरम्।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘उग्रतपाः’ का विसर्ग ‘बुद्ध्वा’ के घोष ‘ब्’ से पहले लुप्त हुआ है (उग्रतपा बुद्ध्वा)। ‘बुद्ध्वा शरण्यम्’ का अर्थ है ‘उन्हें शरण देने योग्य जानकर’।

card.rule: दीर्घं जीवितम् अन्विच्छन् भरद्वाजः इन्द्रम् उपागमत् = Seeking a long life, Bharadvāja approached Indra, having understood that he was fit to give refuge.
card.limits: The verse gives Bharadvāja's aim and his choice of Indra; how Indra came to hold the science is told in the next verses.

concepts.question: Who goes to whom, and what does he want?

concepts.title: ४. ब्रह्मणा हि यथाप्रोक्तम्

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ४। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

words.gram: पु. द्वितीया ए.व. (‘आयुर्वेदम्’ का विशेषण); यथा + प्रोक्तम्, क्रियाविशेषण रूप में भी पढ़ा जा सकता है

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: क्योंकि ब्रह्मा ने जैसा आयुर्वेद कहा था, उसे पहले प्रजापति ने सम्पूर्ण रूप से ग्रहण किया; फिर उनसे दोनों अश्विनीकुमारों ने (ग्रहण किया)।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: For Prajapati first received Ayurveda (the science of life) in its entirety just as it had been proclaimed by Brahma; then the Ashvins in turn (received it) from him.

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: परम्परा की पहली कड़ियाँ: ब्रह्मा ने कहा, प्रजापति ने उसे सम्पूर्ण रूप से ग्रहण किया, फिर अश्विनीकुमारों ने उनसे (ग्रहण किया)। ‘निखिलेन’ का अर्थ ‘पूरा का पूरा’ और ‘आदौ’ का ‘सबसे पहले’ है। ‘जग्राह’ एक ही बार आया है; ‘अश्विनौ’ के साथ उसे दोबारा जोड़कर पढ़ना पड़ता है।

aids.label: क्रम-कड़ी
aids.text: ब्रह्मा → प्रजापति → अश्विनौ। पहले अक्षर: ब्र-प्र-अ।

aids.label: चित्र-शब्द (मेरा बनाया चित्र)
aids.text: ब्रह्मा से अश्विनौ तक = रिले-दौड़ की बैटन: ब्रह्मा से प्रजापति को, प्रजापति से दो घुड़सवारों को।

aids.label: ध्वनि-साम्य (केवल सुनने की सहायता)
aids.text: अश्विनौ ≈ ‘अश्वि-नौ’: नाव पर सवार दो घुड़सवार। (केवल याद के लिए; शब्द का अर्थ ‘अश्व वाले दो’ है।)

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: प्रजापति = प्रजा + पति (प्रजा का पालक) · अश्विनौ ← अश्व (घोड़ा) · आयुर्वेद = आयुः + वेद (जीवन का ज्ञान)।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अ/आ + अ/आ → आ: निखिलेन + आदौ → निखिलेनादौ।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: आदौ (‘पहले’, आदि का सप्तमी एकवचन) ≠ अश्विनौ (‘दो अश्विन’, द्विवचन): दोनों -औ पर, अर्थ अलग।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: ब्रह्मणा हि | यथाप्रोक्तम् | आयुर्वेदं | प्रजापतिः ‖ जग्राह | निखिलेन | आदौ | अश्विनौ तु | पुनस्ततः। (श्लोक में छपा ‘पजापतिः’ = प्रजापतिः, स्रोत में ‘र्’ छूटा।)

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: पाठ में ‘पजापतिः’ छपा है; ‘प्रजापतिः’ अपेक्षित है (ब्रह्मा → प्रजापति → अश्विनौ), यहाँ ‘र्’ छूटा लगता है। छन्द नहीं बदलता। यह सुझाव एक ही स्रोत (SARIT) पर आधारित है; दूसरा पाठ-साक्ष्य अभी नहीं देखा गया। ‘यथाप्रोक्तम्’ को क्रियाविशेषण (‘ठीक जैसा कहा गया’) भी पढ़ा जा सकता है; ‘ततः’ का अर्थ ‘उनसे’ या केवल ‘तब’ हो सकता है।

card.rule: ब्रह्मा → प्रजापति → अश्विनौ. Prajāpati received Āyurveda whole, as Brahmā had proclaimed it; then the two Aśvins received it from him.
card.limits: The printed text reads पजापतिः; प्रजापतिः is the expected name (see the note). The verb जग्राह has to be supplied again for the Aśvins.

concepts.question: Through whom did Āyurveda pass from Brahmā to the Aśvins?

concepts.title: ५. अश्विभ्यां भगवाञ्छक्रः

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ५। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

words.gram: पु. प्रथमा ए.व.; तत्पुरुष, क्त प्र-√वच्

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: अश्विनीकुमारों से भगवान् शक्र (इन्द्र) ने उसे सम्पूर्ण रूप से प्राप्त किया। ऋषियों द्वारा कहे जाने पर भरद्वाज इसलिए शक्र के पास गए।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: From the Ashvins the venerable Shakra (Indra) received it in full. Bharadvaja, asked by the sages, therefore approached Shakra.

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: परम्परा की अगली कड़ी: अश्विनीकुमारों से शक्र (इन्द्र) को आयुर्वेद पूरा मिला। फिर कारण जुड़ता है: इन्द्र के पास ज्ञान था, ‘तस्मात्’ (इसीलिए) भरद्वाज उनके पास गए। ‘ऋषिप्रोक्तः’ का अर्थ ‘ऋषियों द्वारा कहा गया’ है। ‘भगवान्’ यहाँ इन्द्र का आदरसूचक विशेषण है।

aids.label: कौन · किसके पास · क्यों
aids.text: कौन: भरद्वाज · किसके पास: शक्र · क्यों: ज्ञान उनके पास था (तस्मात् = इसलिए)।

aids.label: क्रम-कड़ी
aids.text: ब्र-प्र-अ-श-भ: ब्रह्मा → प्रजापति → अश्विनौ → शक्र; और शक्र के पास भरद्वाज।

aids.label: कथा
aids.text: ज्ञान सीढ़ी से उतरा, ब्रह्मा से इन्द्र तक; ऋषियों द्वारा कहे जाने पर (ऋषिप्रोक्तः) भरद्वाज इन्द्र के पास गए।

aids.label: ध्वनि-साम्य (केवल सुनने की सहायता)
aids.text: शक्र ≈ ‘शक्ति’: शक्र वह जो समर्थ है (√शक्)। (ध्वनि-सहारा और मूल धातु एक ही है।)

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: शक्र ← √शक् (समर्थ होना) · प्रतिपेदे ← प्रति + √पद् (पाना) · केवलम् = पूरा।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: त् + श → च्छ: तस्मात् + शक्रम् → तस्माच्छक्रम्।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: यथाप्रोक्तम् (श्लोक ४: जैसा ज्ञान कहा गया) ↔ ऋषिप्रोक्तः (श्लोक ५: ऋषियों द्वारा कहा गया व्यक्ति, भरद्वाज)। दोनों √वच् से; पहले में कहा गया ज्ञान है, दूसरे में कहा गया व्यक्ति।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: अश्विभ्यां | भगवाञ्छक्रः | प्रतिपेदे ह केवलम् ‖ ऋषिप्रोक्तो भरद्वाजः | तस्माच्छक्रम् | उपागमत्।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘केवलम्’ को ‘पूरा (आयुर्वेद)’ विशेषण या ‘पूर्णतः’ क्रियाविशेषण पढ़ा जा सकता है। ‘ऋषिप्रोक्तः’ का भाव ‘ऋषियों द्वारा कहा/प्रेरित’ है। ‘तस्मात्’ का अर्थ ‘इसलिए’ है।

card.rule: अश्विभ्याम् शक्रः प्रतिपेदे केवलम् = Śakra (Indra) received it whole from the Aśvins; ऋषिप्रोक्तः भरद्वाजः तस्मात् शक्रम् उपागमत् = told by the sages, Bharadvāja therefore went to Śakra.
card.limits: ऋषिप्रोक्तः is read as 'told (asked) by the sages'; the verse does not say what they told him.

concepts.question: How did Āyurveda reach Indra, and why does Bharadvāja go to him?

concepts.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन
concepts.title: ६. विघ्नभूता यदा रोगाः

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ६। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

words.gloss: to austerity, fasting, study, celibacy, vows and life

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: जब देहधारियों में रोग उत्पन्न हुए, जो उनके तप, उपवास, अध्ययन, ब्रह्मचर्य, व्रत और आयु में बाधा बन गए,

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: When diseases arose among embodied beings, becoming obstacles to their austerity, fasting, study, celibacy, vows and life,

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: कथा का दूसरा चरण: रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं। ‘विघ्नभूताः’ का अर्थ ‘बाधा बने हुए’ और ‘प्रादुर्भूताः’ का ‘प्रकट हुए’ है। दूसरी पंक्ति का लम्बा समास बताता है कि किन-किन में बाधा आई: तप, उपवास, अध्ययन, ब्रह्मचर्य, व्रत और आयु में। अन्त की ‘-आयुषाम्’ षष्ठी है: ‘इनकी’। वाक्य ‘यदा’ से शुरू होकर श्लोक ७ के ‘तदा’ पर पूरा होता है।

aids.label: यदा–तदा
aids.text: यदा (जब) रोग आए (श्लोक ६) → तदा (तब) ऋषि जुटे (श्लोक ७)। तराजू के दो पलड़े।

aids.label: कथा
aids.text: रोग आए → साधना और जीवन में रुकावट → (श्लोक ७) करुणा से ऋषि जुटे।

aids.label: चित्र-शब्द (मेरा बनाया चित्र)
aids.text: रोग = रास्ते का पत्थर (विघ्न): तप, उपवास, अध्ययन, ब्रह्मचर्य, व्रत और आयु की राह रुक जाती है।

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: प्रादुर्भूत ← प्रादुर्भाव (उत्पत्ति) · शरीरिन् = शरीर + इन् (देह वाला) · विघ्न = रुकावट (विघ्नहर्ता में वही शब्द)।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: विसर्ग → र् (घोष व्यंजन से पहले): प्रादुः + भूताः → प्रादुर्भूताः।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: विघ्नभूताः (बाधा बने) और प्रादुर्भूताः (प्रकट हुए): दोनों के अन्त में ‘भूताः’ = ‘हुए’। पहले में ‘क्या बने’, दूसरे में ‘कैसे आए’।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: विघ्नभूता | यदा रोगाः | प्रादुर्भूताः | शरीरिणाम् ‖ तपोपवासाध्ययन | ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतायुषाम्।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘ब्रह्मचर्यव्रत’ को एक पद (‘ब्रह्मचर्य का व्रत’) भी माना जा सकता है। ‘शरीरिणाम्’ को ‘प्रादुर्भूताः’ के साथ (‘देहधारियों में प्रकट हुए’) या समास के साथ पढ़ा जा सकता है। वाक्य श्लोक ७ में पूरा होता है।

card.rule: When diseases appeared they became obstacles to the embodied beings' austerity, fasting, study, celibacy, vows and life. The sentence begins with यदा and is completed by तदा in verse 7.
card.limits: The long compound is read as separate items; brahmacarya and vrata could also be one ('the vow of celibacy'). The sentence is not complete until verse 7.

concepts.question: What happened to embodied beings, and what did it block?

concepts.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन
concepts.title: ७. तदा भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ७। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: तब प्राणियों के प्रति करुणा को आगे रखकर, पुण्य कर्म करने वाले महर्षि हिमालय के शुभ पार्श्व (ढलान) पर एकत्र हुए।

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: then, putting compassion for living beings foremost, great sages of virtuous deeds assembled on an auspicious slope of the Himalaya.

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: यदा–तदा का दूसरा आधा: रोग आए (श्लोक ६), तब ऋषि जुटे। प्रेरणा ‘अनुक्रोश’ (करुणा) है; ‘पुरस्कृत्य’ का अर्थ ‘आगे रखकर’ है, यानी करुणा उनके कार्य का पहला कारण है। ‘भूतेषु’ सप्तमी है: प्राणियों के प्रति। स्थान हिमालय का शुभ पार्श्व है। ‘समेताः’ का अर्थ ‘इकट्ठे हुए’ और ‘महर्षयः’ महा + ऋषयः है।

aids.label: कौन · किसके पास · क्यों
aids.text: कौन: महर्षि · कहाँ: हिमालय का शुभ पार्श्व · क्यों: प्राणियों पर करुणा।

aids.label: यदा–तदा
aids.text: तदा (तब) ← यदा (जब), श्लोक ६। रोग आए → तब ऋषि जुटे।

aids.label: कथा
aids.text: रोग फैले → ऋषियों में करुणा जगी → वे हिमालय के ढलान पर एकत्र हुए।

aids.label: चित्र-शब्द (मेरा बनाया चित्र)
aids.text: पुरस्कृत्य = आगे रखकर: जैसे आगे रखी मशाल, वैसे करुणा को आगे रखकर ऋषि एकत्र हुए।

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: अनुक्रोश = दया (अनु + क्रोश) · महर्षि = महा + ऋषि · समेताः = इकट्ठे हुए (सम् + √इ)।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: उ + स्वर → व् + स्वर: भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् → भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: बुद्ध्वा (श्लोक ३) और पुरस्कृत्य (श्लोक ७): दोनों ‘करके’ वाले रूप। अकेली धातु + क्त्वा → ‘-त्वा’ (बुध् → बुद्ध्वा); उपसर्ग या पुरस् जैसे पूर्वपद के साथ → ल्यप् ‘-य’, और ह्रस्व-स्वर वाली धातु के बाद ‘-त्य’ (पुरस् + कृ → पुरस्कृत्य; पर उप + आ + गम् → उपागम्य)।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: तदा | भूतेष्वनुक्रोशं | पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः ‖ समेताः | पुण्यकर्माणः | पार्श्वे हिमवतः शुभे।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: यह वाक्य श्लोक ६ से चला आता है; ऋषियों के नाम श्लोक ८ से आगे हैं। ‘पार्श्व’ का अर्थ बगल या ढलान है।

card.rule: तदा … = Then, putting compassion for living beings foremost, great sages of virtuous deeds assembled on an auspicious slope of the Himālaya.
card.limits: पार्श्वे is read as the 'slope' or side of the mountain; the verse names no peak beyond the Himālaya. The sages' names follow in the next verses.

concepts.question: Who gathered, where, and moved by what?

concepts.title: ८. अङ्गिरा जमदग्निश्च

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ८। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

blocks.label: श्लोक
lines: आत्रेयो गौतमः साङ्ख्यः पुलस्त्यो नारदो ऽसितः ॥ ८ ॥

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: अङ्गिरा, जमदग्नि, वसिष्ठ, कश्यप, भृगु, आत्रेय, गौतम, साङ्ख्य, पुलस्त्य, नारद, असित,

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Angiras, Jamadagni, Vasishtha, Kashyapa, Bhrigu, Atreya, Gautama, Sankhya, Pulastya, Narada, Asita,

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: यहाँ से जुटे हुए ऋषियों की सूची शुरू होती है, जो आगे के श्लोकों में चलती है। पहली पंक्ति में पाँच नाम हैं और दूसरी में छह। ‘नारदो ऽसितः’ का अर्थ नारदः + असितः है; ऽ चिह्न बताता है कि असितः का आरम्भिक ‘अ’ लुप्त हुआ है। पूर्ण सूची के लिए अगले श्लोक देखें।

aids.label: पहले अक्षर
aids.text: पहली पंक्ति: अ-ज-व-क-भृ · दूसरी: आ-गौ-सा-पु-ना-अ (नामों के पहले अक्षर)।

aids.label: ध्वनि-साम्य (केवल सुनने की सहायता)
aids.text: नारदो ऽसितः ≈ ‘नारद-ओ-असित’: बीच का ‘ओ’ याद दिलाता है कि विसर्ग ‘ओ’ बना और ‘अ’ छिप गया। (केवल सुनने की सहायता।)

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: भृगु → भार्गव (भृगु-वंश, श्लोक १०) · आत्रेय ← अत्रि का वंशज (श्लोक २)।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अः + अ → ओ + ऽ (अ के बाद विसर्ग, फिर अ): नारदः + असितः → नारदो ऽसितः (ऽ = छिपा ‘अ’)।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: आत्रेय: श्लोक २ का वक्ता और श्लोक ८ का नाम (नाम वही; वही व्यक्ति या नहीं, यह श्लोक नहीं कहता)। श्लोक ९ में ‘भिक्षु आत्रेय’ एक और नाम माना गया है (दो नाम भी पढ़े जा सकते हैं: पाठ-टिप्पणी)।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: अङ्गिरा जमदग्निश्च | वसिष्ठः कश्यपो भृगुः ‖ आत्रेयो गौतमः साङ्ख्यः | पुलस्त्यो नारदो ऽसितः।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।
lines: आत्रेयो गौतमः साङ्ख्यः | पुलस्त्यो नारदो ऽसितः

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: ‘साङ्ख्यः’ व्यक्ति का नाम भी हो सकता है और ‘साङ्ख्य-आचार्य’ भी; ‘गौतमः साङ्ख्यः’ को एक व्यक्ति भी पढ़ा जा सकता है। यह कार्ड इन्हें दो नाम मानता है। ‘अङ्गिराः’ का विसर्ग ‘ज’ से पहले लुप्त हुआ है।

card.rule: अङ्गिरा, जमदग्नि, वसिष्ठ, कश्यप, भृगु | आत्रेय, गौतम, साङ्ख्य, पुलस्त्य, नारद, असित.
card.limits: साङ्ख्य may be a personal name or a title ('the Sāṅkhya teacher'), and गौतमः साङ्ख्यः might be one person; this card reads them as two names.

concepts.question: Which sages does verse 8 name, in what order?

concepts.title: ९. अगस्त्यो वामदेवश्च

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक ९। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: अगस्त्य, वामदेव, मार्कण्डेय और आश्वलायन, पारिक्षि, भिक्षु आत्रेय, भरद्वाज, कपिञ्जल,

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Agastya, Vamadeva, Markandeya and Ashvalayana, Parikshi, Atreya the mendicant (Bhikshu Atreya), Bharadvaja, Kapinjala,

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: सूची आगे बढ़ती है। ‘मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ’ द्विवचन का द्वन्द्व है: दो नाम एक शब्द में, अन्त में ‘-औ’। ‘भिक्षुरात्रेयः’ = भिक्षुः + आत्रेयः; इसे यहाँ एक व्यक्ति (भिक्षु आत्रेय) पढ़ा गया है। ‘भरद्वाज’ वही नाम है जो श्लोक ३ में आया था। ‘कपिञ्जलः’ का पाठभेद ‘कपिष्ठलः’ है (पाठ-टिप्पणी देखें)।

aids.label: पहले अक्षर
aids.text: अ-वा-मा-आ | पा-भि-भ-क (अगस्त्य, वामदेव, मार्कण्डेय, आश्वलायन | पारिक्षि, भिक्षु आत्रेय, भरद्वाज, कपिञ्जल)।

aids.label: ध्वनि-साम्य (केवल सुनने की सहायता)
aids.text: कपिञ्जल ≈ ‘कपि + जल’: बन्दर और पानी। (केवल याद के लिए; नाम का अर्थ यह नहीं है।)

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: भरद्वाज: वही नाम जो श्लोक ३ में आया · आश्वलायन ← अश्वल का वंशज · मार्कण्डेय ← मृकण्डु का वंशज।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: अ + आ → आ: मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायन (+ द्विवचन -औ) → मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ · विसर्ग → र् (स्वर से पहले): भिक्षुः + आत्रेयः → भिक्षुरात्रेयः।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: आदौ (श्लोक ४, ‘पहले’, एकवचन) ≠ मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ (‘दो ऋषि’, द्विवचन): दोनों -औ पर, अर्थ अलग।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: अगस्त्यो वामदेवश्च | मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ ‖ पारिक्षिर्भिक्षुरात्रेयो | भरद्वाजः कपिञ्जलः।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: पाठभेद: ‘कपिञ्जलः’ की जगह ‘कपिष्ठलः’। ‘भिक्षुरात्रेयः’ को एक व्यक्ति (भिक्षु आत्रेय) माना गया है; दो नाम भी पढ़े जा सकते हैं। ‘पारिक्षि’ की जगह ‘पारीक्षि’ वर्तनी सम्भव है (स्रोत के पाठभेदों में नहीं दी गई)।

card.rule: अगस्त्य, वामदेव, मार्कण्डेय और आश्वलायन, पारिक्षि, भिक्षु आत्रेय, भरद्वाज, कपिञ्जल.
card.limits: The edition notes the variant कपिष्ठलः for कपिञ्जलः. भिक्षुरात्रेयः is read as one person, Bhikṣu Ātreya, though it could be two names.

concepts.question: Which sages does verse 9 add to the list?

concepts.title: १०. विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ च

blocks.label: संदर्भ
blocks.text: चरकसंहिता · सूत्रस्थान · अध्याय १ · श्लोक १०। पाठ: SARIT (एक ही स्रोत)। हिन्दी और English: AI-रचित, AI-समीक्षित; विद्वान् से जाँच शेष।

blocks.label: हिन्दी
blocks.text: विश्वामित्र और आश्मरथ्य, भार्गव च्यवन, अभिजित्, गार्ग्य, शाण्डिल्य और कौण्डिल्य, वार्क्षि, देवल और गालव,

blocks.label: English
blocks.text: Vishvamitra and Ashmarathya, Cyavana the Bhargava, Abhijit, Gargya, Shandilya and Kaundilya, Varkshi, Devala and Galava,

blocks.label: व्याख्या
blocks.text: सूची का यह भाग तीन जोड़ों में बँटा है, जो द्विवचन (-औ) में हैं: विश्वामित्र–आश्मरथ्य, शाण्डिल्य–कौण्डिल्य, देवल–गालव। बीच में एकवचन नाम हैं: भार्गव च्यवन, अभिजित्, गार्ग्य, वार्क्षि। पाठ में एक जगह शब्द-विराम छूटा हुआ दिखता है; इसी कारण यह कार्ड ‘मध्यम विश्वास’ का है (पाठ-टिप्पणी देखें)।

aids.label: पहले अक्षर
aids.text: विश्वामित्र आश्मरथ्य | च्यवन अभिजित् गार्ग्य | शाण्डिल्य कौण्डिल्य | वार्क्षि | देवल गालव (वि-आ | च्य-अ-गा | शा-कौ | वा | दे-गा)।

aids.label: ध्वनि-साम्य (केवल सुनने की सहायता)
aids.text: गालव ≈ ‘गाल + व’, देवल ≈ ‘देव + ल’: दो छोटे सुनने के हुक। (अर्थ से कोई सम्बन्ध नहीं।)

aids.label: शब्द-परिवार
aids.text: वंश-नाम: भार्गव ← भृगु · गार्ग्य ← गर्ग · आत्रेय ← अत्रि।

aids.label: संधि-नियम
aids.text: विसर्ग + च → श्: भार्गवः + च्यवनः → भार्गवश्च्यवनः।

aids.label: मिलते-जुलते की जोड़ी
aids.text: तीन जोड़े (-औ): विश्वामित्र–आश्मरथ्य · शाण्डिल्य–कौण्डिल्य · देवल–गालव; बाकी नाम अकेले: च्यवन, अभिजित्, गार्ग्य, वार्क्षि।

aids.label: लय में खण्ड
aids.text: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ च | भार्गवश्च्यवनो ऽभिजित् ‖ गार्ग्यः | शाण्डिल्यकौण्डिल्यौ | वार्क्षिर्देवलगालवौ।

aids.label: छन्द
aids.text: हर पंक्ति में ८ + ८ अक्षर (गिनती से)। ‘|’ पाद की सीमा है; संधि के कारण वह शब्द के बीच भी पड़ सकती है।

blocks.label: पाठ-टिप्पणी
blocks.text: विश्वास: मध्यम। (१) ‘शाण्डिल्यकौण्डिल्यौवार्क्षिः’ में शब्द-विराम छूटा हो सकता है (शाण्डिल्यकौण्डिल्यौ वार्क्षिः); इससे पाठ नहीं बदलता। (२) पाठभेद: ‘कौण्डिन्यौ’। (३) ‘भार्गवश्च्यवनः’ को एक व्यक्ति माना गया है; दो नाम भी हो सकते हैं। (४) ‘आश्मरथ्य’ को ‘अश्मरथ्य’ भी पढ़ा जा सकता है (सम्भावित, स्रोत के पाठभेदों में नहीं)।

card.rule: Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya, Cyavana the Bhārgava, Abhijit, Gārgya, Śāṇḍilya and Kauṇḍilya, Vārkṣi, Devala and Gālava.
card.limits: A word space may be missing in …कौण्डिल्यौवार्क्षिः…; the edition notes the variant कौण्डिन्य; भार्गवश्च्यवनः is read as one person (it could be two); आश्मरथ्य could also be अश्मरथ्य.

concepts.question: Who else is named in verse 10, and which readings are uncertain?

questions.q: The sentence अथातो दीर्घञ्जीवितीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः opens a chapter. What does it announce?
options: A chapter on long life will now be expounded
A king's order for a journey
A list of diseases and their cures
optionExplain: Right: It names the chapter, and says it will be explained.
Nothing here concerns a king or a journey.
No disease is named in this sentence.
No god is addressed; the sentence introduces a chapter.
questions.explain: अध्यायं (chapter) and व्याख्यास्यामः (we shall expound) show that a chapter is being introduced.
questions.rule: The opening sentence names the chapter and promises to explain it.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening sentence to its meaning.
questions.explain: These four words carry the whole announcement.
questions.rule: अथ = now; अतः = therefore; अध्यायम् = chapter; व्याख्यास्यामः = we shall expound.

questions.q: The word for 'chapter' in the sentence is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The sentence says अध्यायम् for 'chapter'.
questions.teaches: अध्यायम् ends in -म्, the accusative: the chapter is what is being expounded, the object of the verb.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अथातः?
optionExplain: There is no word तः here.
Right: अ + अ gives आ, so अथ + अतः is written अथातः.
आतः is not a word in this sentence.
थातः is not a word.
questions.explain: अथातः is अथ ('now') + अतः ('therefore') joined by sandhi.

questions.q: व्याख्यास्यामः ends in -मः. Who is speaking, and how many?
options: He, one teacher: third person singular
You, the students: second person plural
We, the teachers: first person plural
They, the sages: third person plural
optionExplain: The third person singular would end in -ति.
The second person plural would end in -थ.
Right: -मः marks 'we', and the future sense gives 'we shall'.
The third person plural would end in -न्ति.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the first person plural future: 'we shall expound'.

questions.q: Another chapter opens अथातो मात्राशितीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः. What is the same as here, and what changes?
options: Everything changes, since each chapter opens in its own way
Only व्याख्यास्यामः stays; the other words change
Only the chapter name changes; the frame stays
optionExplain: The frame is shared; only the name sits in the middle.
अथातः and अध्यायम् stay too.
व्याख्यास्यामः stays 'we shall expound'.
Right: Chapters of this part share the frame अथातो … अध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.explain: The name in the middle (here मात्राशितीयम्) is the only part that changes.
questions.rule: The opening frame is shared; the title sits in the middle.
questions.teaches: Once you know the frame, you can read any chapter title by looking at the word before अध्यायम्.

questions.q: In इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः, who is named as the speaker?
optionExplain: Right: आत्रेयः is the last word, in the nominative: he is the one who spoke.
Bharadvāja is named in the next verse, not here.
Indra is named in the next verse, not here.
Prajāpati comes later in the story.
questions.explain: The speaker is भगवान् आत्रेयः, the venerable Ātreya.
questions.rule: इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः = 'Thus said the venerable Ātreya.'

questions.q: Match each word of the line to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words make up a fixed attribution formula.
questions.rule: इति = thus; ह = indeed; आह = said; भगवान् = the venerable.

questions.q: The verb meaning 'said' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: The verb of the line is आह, joined to स्म as स्माह.
questions.teaches: आह is a past form of the root √अह्: 'he said'. It tells you one speaker, in the past.

questions.q: Which is the right split of स्माह?
optionExplain: ह is a separate word earlier in the line.
Right: म् + आ joins as मा, so स्म + आह is written स्माह.
माह is not a word.
The verb is आह, with a long आ.
questions.explain: स्माह is the particle स्म followed by the verb आह.

questions.q: Whose words are 'we shall expound' in the opening sentence, and what shows it?
options: The compiler's own; the text speaks in its own voice
Ātreya's; इति closes the sentence as his quoted words
Bharadvāja's; he is the seeker of verse 3
optionExplain: इति ह स्माह hands the words to Ātreya.
Indra is not the speaker of this line.
Right: इति marks the end of a quotation and the next line names the speaker.
Bharadvāja appears only after this line.
questions.explain: इति … आह ties the opening sentence to Ātreya.
questions.rule: इति closes a quotation; आह names its speaker.

questions.q: Many chapters repeat this second line after a new title. What does it tell you about such a chapter?
options: The speaker has changed to the new title's sage
It is a later addition by the compiler
It marks the chapter as written in verse
The teaching is again given as Ātreya's
optionExplain: The formula names Ātreya, not a new speaker.
Nothing in the line says it was added later.
The line says who spoke, not what form the chapter takes.
Right: The same formula hands the new chapter to the same speaker.
questions.explain: The repeated line works as a signature: it keeps Ātreya as the voice of the teaching.
questions.rule: A repeated इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः = the same voice again.
questions.teaches: A repeated formula is a signature: it tells you whose teaching you are reading.

questions.q: Bharadvāja wants a long life and goes to a god for help. Whom do you expect him to approach?
optionExplain: Right: The verse names Indra, with the title अमरेश्वरम्.
Brahmā taught earlier; the verse does not send Bharadvāja to him.
Yama is not mentioned in this verse.
Agni is not mentioned in this verse.
questions.explain: Bharadvāja approached Indra, the lord of the immortals.
questions.rule: Bharadvāja goes to Indra for a long life.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words give what Bharadvāja wants and what he is like.
questions.rule: दीर्घम् = long; जीवितम् = life; उग्रतपाः = of severe austerity; शरण्यम् = fit to give refuge.

questions.q: The word for 'having understood' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: बुद्ध्वा comes from the root √बुध्, 'to understand'.
questions.teaches: बुद्ध्वा is a 'having done' word (the -त्वा type): it names an action finished before the main verb. He understood, then he approached.

questions.q: Which is the right split of अमरेश्वरम्?
optionExplain: श्वरम् is not a word.
Right: अ + ई joins as ए, so अमर + ईश्वरम् is written अमरेश्वरम्.
Neither part is a word.
The second word begins with ई, not ऐ.
questions.explain: अमरेश्वरम् = अमर (immortal) + ईश्वरम् (lord): the lord of the immortals.

questions.q: A reader says Indra went to Bharadvāja. Which word in the verse shows this is wrong?
options: इन्द्रम्: its ending -म् marks Indra as the doer
भरद्वाज: it is an accusative, so Bharadvāja is approached
इन्द्रम्: its ending -म् marks Indra as the one approached
उपागमत् is future: nothing has happened yet
optionExplain: -म् on such a name marks the one approached, not the doer.
भरद्वाज is the doer; its -ः is dropped by sandhi before उपागमत्.
Right: For a masculine name in -अ, -म् is the accusative: the one approached.
उपागमत् is a past form: he approached.
questions.explain: इन्द्रम् (-म्) is the object of उपागमत्; भरद्वाजः is the doer (its -ः disappears by sandhi before उपागमत्).
questions.rule: Masculine name in -अ: doer -ः (or -ो / dropped, by sandhi), the one approached -म्.

questions.q: An invented line reads वसिष्ठो वरुणमुपागमत्. By the same pattern, who goes to whom?
optionExplain: That would need the endings the other way round.
Nothing joins them as doers.
उपागमत् says that a going took place.
Right: वसिष्ठो is वसिष्ठः joined by sandhi: the doer; वरुणम् (-म्) is the one approached.
questions.explain: The pattern of verse 3 carries over to any name with the same endings.
questions.rule: Doer name (-ः / -ो) + object name (-म्) + उपागमत् = the first goes to the second.
questions.teaches: For masculine names in -अ you can read who goes to whom from the endings: -ः (or -ो) for the doer, -म् for the one approached.

questions.q: Brahmā proclaimed Āyurveda. Who do you expect received it first?
optionExplain: Right: The verse names Prajāpati as the first receiver.
Indra comes later, in verse 5.
They receive it from Prajāpati, so they come second.
Bharadvāja comes at the end of the chain.
questions.explain: Prajāpati received it first, then the Aśvins.

questions.q: Put the three in the order the knowledge passed, starting with the one who proclaimed it.
questions.explain: Each one receives from the one before.

questions.q: The word meaning 'in its entirety' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: निखिलेन means 'entirely'.
questions.teaches: निखिलेन ends in -एन, the instrumental, used like an adverb: 'by the whole', so 'completely'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of निखिलेनादौ?
optionExplain: नादौ is not a word.
Right: अ + आ joins as आ, so निखिलेन + आदौ is written निखिलेनादौ.
दौ is not a word.
The second word is आदौ, 'in the beginning'.
questions.explain: निखिलेनादौ = निखिलेन ('entirely') + आदौ ('at first').

questions.q: जग्राह appears once, yet the Aśvins also receive. What lets us read it that way?
options: अश्विनौ is itself a verb meaning 'received'
ब्रह्मणा is the doer of both
The verb is understood again for अश्विनौ
The verse is incomplete and cannot be read
optionExplain: अश्विनौ is a name, in the dual.
ब्रह्मणा names who proclaimed, not who received.
Right: अश्विनौ has no verb of its own, so जग्राह is carried over to it.
It reads fully once the verb is carried over.
questions.explain: Sanskrit often leaves a verb out when the same one fits again; here जग्राह is understood again, in the dual, for the two Aśvins.
questions.rule: A verb can be understood again for a second doer.

questions.q: An invented line reads वसिष्ठेन यथोक्तं ज्ञानं शिष्यो जग्राह. Who spoke, and who received?
optionExplain: The endings are the other way round.
शिष्यः is the one who received.
यथोक्तम् says it was spoken.
Right: वसिष्ठेन (-एन) names who spoke; शिष्यः is the doer of जग्राह.
questions.explain: The same pattern as ब्रह्मणा यथाप्रोक्तम् … जग्राह: -एन/-णा names the speaker.
questions.rule: The speaker ends in -एन/-णा; the receiver is the doer of जग्राह.
questions.teaches: An -एन / -णा name before a 'spoken' word is the speaker.

questions.q: From whom did Indra (Śakra) receive Āyurveda?
optionExplain: Right: अश्विभ्याम् gives the Aśvins as the source.
Brahmā comes before Prajāpati in the chain.
Prajāpati gave it to the Aśvins, not to Indra.
Bharadvāja comes to Indra to receive it.
questions.explain: Indra received it from the Aśvins.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words carry the handing over from the Aśvins to Indra.
questions.rule: अश्विभ्याम् = from the Aśvins; शक्रः = Śakra (Indra); केवलम् = wholly.

questions.q: In this verse the word meaning 'therefore' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: तस्मात् gives the reason: Indra had the science, so Bharadvāja went to him.
questions.teaches: तस्मात् is the -आत् form of तद् ('that'): 'from that', so 'for that reason'.

questions.q: Which is the right split of तस्माच्छक्रमुपागमत्?
optionExplain: च्छक्रम् is not a word.
Right: त् + श् joins as च्छ्, and म् + उ as मु; the three words come back.
The name is शक्र, not छक्र.
The verb is उपागमत्, with उ.
questions.explain: तस्माच्छक्रमुपागमत् = तस्मात् ('therefore') + शक्रम् ('Śakra') + उपागमत् ('approached').

questions.q: Which line gives the order of transmission in verses 4 and 5?
optionExplain: Prajāpati comes before the Aśvins.
Brahmā is the first, not the second.
Right: Each receives from the one before, as verses 4 and 5 say.
Śakra receives from the Aśvins, not before them.
questions.explain: The chain of verses 4 and 5 is Brahmā, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Śakra.

questions.q: ऋषिप्रोक्तः means 'told (asked) by the sages'. By the same pattern, what does गुरुप्रोक्तः mean?
optionExplain: The teacher is the one who tells, not the one told.
The compound describes what was told.
It is not a pair; the first member says by whom.
Right: The first member names the one who tells; the second is 'told'.
questions.explain: A first member like ऋषि- or गुरु- names the one by whom something was told.
questions.teaches: In X-प्रोक्तः the first member names the speaker, as in ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्तम् (verse 4).

questions.q: The verse speaks of diseases as विघ्नभूताः. Which meaning of विघ्न do you expect?
optionExplain: Right: विघ्न means an obstacle or hindrance.
Medicine would be the opposite of what the verse says.
The sages come in the next verse.
No teacher is meant here.
questions.explain: Diseases became obstacles (विघ्न) to the practices named in the second line.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words tell what happened and to whom.
questions.rule: विघ्नभूताः = having become obstacles; प्रादुर्भूताः = arose; शरीरिणाम् = of embodied beings; यदा = when.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The word for 'of embodied beings' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: शरीरिणाम् names those who have a body.
questions.teaches: -णाम् is the genitive plural, 'of ...'. शरीरिन् means 'one who has a body', so शरीरिणाम् is 'of the embodied'.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Which is the right split of प्रादुर्भूताः?
optionExplain: There is no अ in front of भूताः.
Right: A visarga before the voiced भ becomes र्, so प्रादुः + भूताः is written प्रादुर्भूताः.
र्भूताः is not a word.
आदुर्भूताः is not a word.
questions.explain: प्रादुर्भूताः = प्रादुः ('into view') + भूताः ('become'): they came into being.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The second line ends in -आयुषाम्, a genitive plural. On the usual reading, what does that say about the list?
options: These are the people who study
These are the things the diseases got in the way of
These are the sages who gather
optionExplain: The diseases are रोगाः in the first line.
The people are शरीरिणाम्.
Right: 'Of austerity ... and life': the genitive links the list to the obstacles.
The sages gather in verse 7.
questions.explain: The list in the genitive names what the obstacles are for: practices and life itself.
questions.rule: The genitive list = what was obstructed.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: A sentence begins यदा रोगाः प्रादुर्भूताः. Which word would begin the clause that completes it?
optionExplain: कदा asks 'when?'; it does not answer यदा.
यथा pairs with तथा, 'as ... so'.
तथा means 'so, likewise', not 'then'.
Right: यदा … तदा is the matching pair: 'when ... then'.
questions.explain: यदा 'when' is answered by तदा 'then'; verse 7 begins with तदा.
questions.teaches: Sanskrit pairs words like यदा–तदा and यथा–तथा; seeing one tells you which will answer it.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Diseases have appeared. What do you expect moved the great sages to assemble?
options: A plan to hold a sacrifice
optionExplain: Right: The verse says they put compassion first.
No command is mentioned.
Nothing of the kind is said.
No sacrifice is mentioned.
questions.explain: They assembled out of compassion (अनुक्रोश) for living beings.
questions.rule: अनुक्रोश = compassion, the reason they gathered.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These words say why and how the sages met.
questions.rule: अनुक्रोशम् = compassion; पुरस्कृत्य = putting foremost; समेताः = assembled; शुभे = auspicious.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: The word for 'great sages' is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: महर्षयः are the doers of the assembling.
questions.teaches: महर्षयः = महा + ऋषयः, and -अयः is the nominative plural: the sages are the subject.
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Which is the right split of भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्?
optionExplain: भूतेष्व is not a word.
Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्, so भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् is written भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम्.
वनुक्रोशम् is not a word.
षु is only an ending, not a word.
questions.explain: भूतेष्वनुक्रोशम् = भूतेषु ('for beings') + अनुक्रोशम् ('compassion').
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: भूतेषु ends in -षु, the locative plural. How does it relate to the compassion?
options: It is felt by the beings
It is felt toward the beings
optionExplain: The doer would end differently.
'From' would need the ablative.
Right: The locative gives the one at whom the feeling is directed.
questions.explain: भूतेषु + अनुक्रोशम् = compassion toward living beings.
questions.rule: Locative of the object of a feeling = 'toward' (the locative itself means 'in, among').
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: In verse 3, बुद्ध्वा named an earlier act (having understood). By the same pattern, what is true of पुरस्कृत्य?
options: It is a noun naming a place
It is a verb in the future tense
It names an earlier act, and its doer is the sages
optionExplain: The place is पार्श्वे.
It does not end like a future.
Indra is not in this verse.
Right: -त्य ends a 'having done' word, as -त्वा does, with the same doer as the main sentence.
questions.explain: बुद्ध्वा and पुरस्कृत्य are the same kind of word: an earlier act by the same doer.
questions.rule: -त्वा / -त्य words = 'having done', with the sentence's own doer.
questions.teaches: -त्वा and -त्य both mean 'having done'; -त्य is used when a prefix comes before the root (पुरस्-कृ).
questions.section: रोगों का आना, ऋषियों का सम्मेलन

questions.q: Verse 8 begins a list of sages. Which of these names do you expect in it?
optionExplain: Right: Vasiṣṭha is one of the sages of the list.
Indra is a god, not one of the gathered sages.
Prajāpati is a god in the chain of verse 4.
The Aśvins are the twin gods of verse 4.
questions.explain: The list names sages; the gods of the chain (Brahmā, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Indra) are not in it.

questions.q: Put these four names in the order of verse 8.
questions.explain: These four follow अङ्गिरा in the first line.

questions.q: In the first line the name after कश्यपः is ____ (type it in Devanagari).
questions.explain: भृगुः closes the first line.
questions.teaches: भृगुः is the last name of the first line; the second line opens with आत्रेयः.
questions.rule: Line 1 ends with भृगुः; line 2 begins with आत्रेयः.

questions.q: Which gives the two words of नारदो ऽसितः before sandhi?
optionExplain: The original ending is -ः; ो comes from the join.
Right: -ः before अ becomes ो, and ऽ marks the dropped अ.
The name is असित, with its अ.
दोऽसितः is not a word.
questions.explain: नारदो ऽसितः = नारदः + असितः: two names.

questions.q: Taking साङ्ख्यः as a separate name, which comes right after गौतमः in verse 8?
optionExplain: पुलस्त्यः comes after साङ्ख्यः.
नारदः comes near the end of the line.
Right: The second line runs आत्रेयः, गौतमः, साङ्ख्यः.
असितः is the last name.
questions.explain: आत्रेयः → गौतमः → साङ्ख्यः → पुलस्त्यः → नारदः → असितः.

questions.q: आत्रेयः appears in the second line of this verse. Where did you meet the same name earlier in the chapter?
options: In verse 3, as the one who approached Indra
In verse 4, as the first receiver
In the opening formula इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः
optionExplain: Verse 3 names Bharadvāja.
Verse 4 names Prajāpati.
Verse 6 names diseases, not people.
Right: Line 2 of the chapter names Ātreya as the speaker.
questions.explain: The same name occurs again; the verse does not say whether it is the same person.
questions.rule: आत्रेयः: the speaker named in line 2 and a name in verse 8 (same name; same person is not stated).
questions.teaches: A name can recur in a text; check where else you have met it before deciding it is new.

questions.q: One name in verse 9 is a sage you met in verse 3. Which do you expect?
optionExplain: Right: Bharadvāja, who approached Indra in verse 3, is named again.
Indra is a god, not one of the sages.
Prajāpati is a god in the chain of verse 4.
Śakra is another name of Indra.
questions.explain: भरद्वाजः appears in the list.
questions.rule: भरद्वाजः is in verse 3 and again in the list of verse 9.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading the names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: अगस्त्यः = Agastya; वामदेवः = Vāmadeva; पारिक्षिः = Pārikṣi; कपिञ्जलः = Kapiñjala.

questions.q: The ending -औ on a name like मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ shows that it names ____ sages (type the number).
questions.explain: -औ is the dual ending: two items in one word.
questions.teaches: On names in -अ, -औ marks the dual. मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ joins two names, Mārkaṇḍeya and Āśvalāyana. (Do not confuse आदौ in verse 4: that is the locative singular of आदि.)

questions.q: Which is the right split of मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ?
optionExplain: श्वलायनौ is not a name.
Right: -अ + आ- merge into आ, so मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायनौ is written मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ.
याश्वलायनौ is not a name.
Sandhi alone cannot tell अ + अ from अ + आ here, but the sage's name is आश्वलायन, with a long आ.
questions.explain: मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ = मार्कण्डेय + आश्वलायनौ: two sages.

questions.q: A copy has कपिष्ठलः where this edition has कपिञ्जलः. What kind of difference is this?
options: A different sage in the list
A variant reading of the same name, recorded in the notes
A mistake made by the edition
optionExplain: Nothing in the text adds another name here.
Sandhi changes letters only where two words meet; this difference is inside the name.
Right: The edition itself lists कपिष्ठलः as a variant.
The edition records both readings.
questions.explain: Variant readings of a name are noted, not silently corrected.
questions.rule: कपिञ्जलः / कपिष्ठलः = two readings of the name in the text.

questions.q: A new line reads वसिष्ठभरद्वाजौ. How many sages does it name, and why?
options: One, because it is a single compound name
Three, because the word is long
Two, because -औ is the dual ending
optionExplain: -औ would not appear on a single name like that.
Length does not count names.
The ending tells you.
Right: The dual joins वसिष्ठ and भरद्वाज in one word.
questions.explain: The dual ending -औ works with any pair of names in -अ.
questions.teaches: You can count the items in a dual compound from the ending, even for names you have not met.

questions.q: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ ends in -औ, like मार्कण्डेयाश्वलायनौ in verse 9. How many sages do you expect it to name?
optionExplain: Right: On names in -अ, -औ marks a pair (the dual).
A single name would not take -औ here.
-औ is for two, not three.
-औ is for two, not four.
questions.explain: विश्वामित्राश्मरथ्यौ names two sages: Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya.

questions.q: Match each Devanagari name to its Latin spelling.
questions.explain: Reading these names in Devanagari is the point of this card.
questions.rule: च्यवनः = Cyavana; गार्ग्यः = Gārgya; वार्क्षिः = Vārkṣi; गालवः = Gālava.

questions.q: Complete the last pair of the verse: देवल और ____ (type the name in Devanagari).
questions.explain: देवलगालवौ is the last pair of the verse.
questions.teaches: देवलगालवौ is a dual compound of देवल and गालव, and it closes the verse.

questions.q: Which is the right split of भार्गवश्च्यवनः?
optionExplain: श्च्यवनः is not a name.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, so भार्गवः + च्यवनः is written भार्गवश्च्यवनः.
The name is च्यवन, with च.
श् is not a word-ending that stands on its own.
questions.explain: भार्गवश्च्यवनः = भार्गवः ('the Bhārgava') + च्यवनः (Cyavana).

questions.q: Which of these are dual pairs in verse 10?
optionExplain: Right: -औ names Viśvāmitra and Āśmarathya.
A single name, with -ः.
Right: -औ names Śāṇḍilya and Kauṇḍilya.
Right: -औ names Devala and Gālava.
A single name.
questions.explain: Three words end in -औ and name pairs; the other two are single names.

questions.q: In another book you find कौण्डिन्य where verse 10 has कौण्डिल्य. What should you conclude?
options: Likely the same name spelt differently; check the note
Nothing can be said about it
optionExplain: The edition's own note shows both spellings occur for this name.
Neither spelling can be called wrong without evidence.
Right: The edition itself records कौण्डिन्य as a variant of this name.
Variants are recorded precisely so you can compare.
questions.explain: Variant spellings of names are common; compare notes before deciding.
questions.rule: Same name, two spellings: check the variant note first.
questions.teaches: A name spelt differently in another source may be a variant; the edition's note is the first place to look.
